d.t: The quality that renders something desirable or valuable; worth.
d.e: There is tremendous value in a good education.

d.t: (uncountable) The degree of importance given to something.
d.e: The value of my children's happiness is second only to that of my wife.

d.t: (often plural) That which is valued or highly esteemed, such as one's morals, morality, or belief system.
d.e: He does not share his parents' values.

d.t: The amount (of money or goods or services) that is considered to be a fair equivalent for something else.
d.e: The value of the stolen painting is estimated to be around four million pounds.

d.t: (music) The relative duration of a musical note.
d.e: The value of a crotchet is twice that of a quaver.

d.t: (art) The relative darkness or lightness of a color in (a specific area of) a painting etc.
(mathematics, physics) Any definite numerical quantity or other mathematical object, determined by being measured, computed, or otherwise defined.
d.e: The exact value of pi cannot be represented in decimal notation.

d.t: Precise meaning; import.
d.e: the value of a word; the value of a legal instrument

d.t: (in the plural) The valuable ingredients to be obtained by treating a mass or compound; specifically, the precious metals contained in rock, gravel, etc.
(obsolete) Esteem; regard.
(obsolete) Valour.
To determine or estimate the value of; to judge the worth of.
d.e: I will have the family jewels valued by a professional.

d.t: To regard highly; think much of; place importance upon.
d.e: Gold was valued highly among the Romans.

d.t: To hold dear; to cherish.
To a great extent or degree.
Conforming to fact, reality or rule; true.
(with superlatives) Used to firmly establish that nothing else surpasses in some respect.
d.e: He was the very best runner there.

d.t: (literary) True, real, actual.
d.e: the fierce hatred of a very woman

d.t: The same; identical.
d.e: He proposed marriage in the same restaurant, at the very table where they first met.

d.t: With limiting effect: mere.
d.e: The very idea of climbing the ladder brings me out in a sweat.

d.t: (physical) Visual perception.
A picture, drawn or painted; a sketch.
d.e: a fine view of Lake George

d.t: An opinion, judgement, imagination, idea or belief.
(computing, databases) A virtual or logical table composed of the result set of a query in relational databases.
(computing, programming) The part of a computer program which is visible to the user and can be interacted with.
A wake.
(transitive) To look at.
d.e: Reporters viewed a private screening of the upcoming film.

d.t: (transitive) To regard in a stated way.
d.e: I view it as a serious breach of trust.
